Yes, the Light Up a Life tree is coming back to the window this year. Someone asked on our page the other day whether we would be doing it again, and I was very glad to be asked.

For anyone who hasn't done it before, here is how it works. From Monday 16 November there will be memory tags in the shop. You write a name, or a few words, whatever feels right, and we hang it on the tree. The suggested donation is £3 a tag. If you would rather write yours at home, there are envelopes on the counter to take with you, and you can bring the tag in when you're ready.

Seven years ago this month my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the counter with the same pen, and it has become one of the quieter moments of my year. I mention it only so you know the tree is looked after by people who understand what it is to sit down and write one of those.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving. You don't need to have had someone at the hospice. Whoever you are missing is welcome on it.

You also don't need to buy anything or write anything. If you would simply like to come and stand by the tree for a few minutes, please do. That is what it's there for.

We will switch the lights on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is doing her mince pies again. Wrap up warm, and if you can, get there before the pies do. Last year they didn't last past the first carol.

Every name on the tree will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm in the day centre. You are very welcome to come along, but you don't have to. Your person's name will be read either way.

Last year the tree carried 412 names, and Magdalen Street was full of people standing in the cold, which I will not forget. Thank you to everyone who trusted us with a name, who came to the lights, and who stopped to read the tags and had a quiet word with a stranger. It made the shop feel like the right place to be.

Do come in and see us.

Jean
